reviewer: Codex adversarial review with UX state-model verification

adversarialFindings.description: The earlier protocol treated peer notifications as authority and made every open tab read-only, so advisory delivery determined safety and no tab could remain the writer.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Made the Web Locks writer lock authoritative, added shared presence for every participant, and retained messages only for invalidation and liveness.

adversarialFindings.description: The invalidated implementation had uncovered BFCache, revision-token, closing-message, transport-recovery, asynchronous-write, and shutdown transitions.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Bound revision tokens and leases to coordinator identity and write epoch, reconciled every closing revision, forced BFCache rereads, restarted discovery on recovery, and retained the coordinator until active leases settle.

adversarialFindings.description: Underlying lock ownership could be exposed to route controls before application state was fully read and acknowledged.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The provider now derives canWrite as false until its verified application status is ready.

adversarialFindings.description: Every successful UI write triggered automatic route invalidation, erasing route-local success feedback and creating overlapping refresh races.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Added runLocalMutation to suppress the write event during the local mutation and perform one verified post-commit refresh with explicit route-invalidation policy.

adversarialFindings.description: A state-comparison heuristic could misclassify an unwrapped same-owner write as a safe UI write and preserve a stale draft.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Removed the heuristic. Every automatic event invalidates the route; only the explicit local mutation wrapper may preserve it.

adversarialFindings.description: Classic course, session, RPG resource, onboarding, and settings surfaces did not consistently enforce coordination state at every IndexedDB mutation control.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Wrapped all UI mutation entry points, disabled reader writes, retained navigation, and treated export as a write because it records a backup event.

adversarialFindings.description: Startup and stale-state application tests fabricated authority with hello and closing messages instead of contending the authoritative lock.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Added deterministic hold and release controls to the Web Locks fake and rewrote the tests around real lock contention, transfer, and read gates.

adversarialFindings.description: The real-browser settings test asserted that both concurrent pages were read-only and therefore certified the wrong product contract.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The Chromium test now proves one owner can save ordinary settings, the peer is read-only, both pages block destructive operations, and exclusive actions recover after the peer closes.

adversarialFindings.description: The active coordination contract and validation log still described the superseded all-tabs-read-only design and claimed Module 3 was accepted.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Replaced the contract with the Web Locks authority model and marked the historical Module 3 acceptance invalidated with the active count reset to 0/3.

adversarialFindings.description: Release manifests allowed reviewer, adversarial findings, and retrospective fields to remain empty while reporting a passed status.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The runner now requires a tracked, checksummed, module-matched review file with findings, resolutions, reviewer, and a proceeding retrospective.

adversarialFindings.description: Release skip and retry totals were hardcoded to zero, and command records omitted parsed test counts, allowing incomplete suites to look clean.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The runner now parses test counts, skips, pending or todo tests, and retries per command, fails on any exception, and totals measured values.

adversarialFindings.description: The CI workflow labeled every future three-pass run as foundation, making later evidence semantically false even when commands passed.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The workflow now labels all three jobs as module-3-storage-durability and supplies the exact tracked Module 3 review file.

adversarialFindings.description: A contended reader does not automatically consume every owner revision while the owner remains open, so its visible snapshot may lag until manual reload or ownership transfer.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Accepted for Module 3 because writes remain blocked and manual guarded reload is available; continuous reader refresh is a UX enhancement, not a safety prerequisite.

adversarialFindings.description: Browsers without Web Locks cannot create, repair, seed, or mutate the local database under the fail-closed protocol.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Accepted and documented. Compatible existing data remains readable; unsupported browsers expose writing as unavailable rather than falling back to advisory authority.

adversarialFindings.description: The counted Module 3 browser matrix remains Chromium-only; Firefox, WebKit, real-device, and assistive-technology certification is not yet present.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Accepted only as a stage boundary because Module 6 explicitly owns cross-browser and device validation. Module 3 must not claim that later evidence.

adversarialFindings.description: docs/storage-safety.md still described the superseded all-tabs-read-only advisory protocol after M3-AR-09 claimed documentation replacement, contradicting the Web Locks authority contract.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Rewrote the concurrent-tabs section to describe single-writer Web Locks authority, contended read-only peers, exclusive presence for destructive operations, and fail-closed behavior without Web Locks; clarified PRIVACY.md localStorage scope.

retrospective.summary: Do not freeze or count Module 3 yet. The corrected release runner, full browser matrix, documentation, and clean immutable candidate still require verification.
